title: Formalisme algébrique des correspondances et algèbres de Poincaré-Hodge (cf conjectures standard) : notes manuscrites (s.d.), tapuscrit annoté (s.d.), lettres (1966-1967).

deep.reconstruction:
The page, headed 'Algèbres de Hodge d'ordre 2', works out the complete structure of an abstract 'Poincaré–Hodge algebra' of formal dimension 2, i.e. the cohomology of a surface. The ring is graded commutative, with H^0=k, H^1=V, H^2=kξ⊕W (ξ is the polarisation class, W the primitive part), H^3=V^∨ and H^4=kξ².

The data are:
- V and W;
- the cup product Λ²V→H², α(x∧y)=φ(x,y)ξ+ψ(x,y), with φ an alternating form and ψ an alternating bilinear map V×V→W;
- the product Sym²W→kξ², β(ww')=Q(w,w')ξ², with Q symmetric.

Grothendieck claims (V,W,φ,ψ,Q) determine H* up to canonical isomorphism. The remaining products are forced by duality:
- xξ=ξx=φ̃(x)∈V^∨, with ⟨y,φ̃(x)⟩=φ(y,x);
- xw=wx is the functional y↦Q(ψ(y,x),w);
- xy'=−y'x=⟨x,y'⟩ξ² for y'∈V^∨;
- ξ·ξ=ξ², ξw=0 (W is primitive, i.e. orthogonal to ξ), ww'=Q(w,w')ξ².

For any choice of φ,ψ,Q this gives an anticommutative multiplication with unit 1. The products H^1×H^2→H^3 are defined so that y(xa)=(yx)a.

The only genuine associativity constraint is in degree 4 on four degree-1 elements: (xy)(tz)=(tx)(yz). Explicitly:
φ(x,y)φ(t,z)+Q(ψ(x,y),ψ(t,z)) = φ(t,x)φ(y,z)+Q(ψ(t,x),ψ(y,z)).
The marginal note says this is the same as requiring the 4-form (xy)(zt) to be alternating, so that it depends only on x∧y∧z∧t. Equivalently, the symmetric form φ·φ+Q∘(ψ⊗ψ) on Λ²V must lie in Λ⁴V^∨ ⊂ Sym²(Λ²V^∨): its 'algebraic curvature tensor' (Bianchi-type) component must vanish.

The axioms are then translated into conditions on the data:
- Lefschetz: ξ²:H^0≅H^4 always holds; ξ:H^1→H^3 is an isomorphism iff φ is nondegenerate (so dim V is even).
- Poincaré: H^4≅k always holds; the pairings H^0×H^4 and H^1×H^3 are perfect automatically; H^2×H^2→H^4 is perfect iff Q is nondegenerate (the Gram matrix is diag(1,Q)).

The positivity (Hodge-index) axiom is not yet treated on this page. The page is a test case for Grothendieck's axiomatics of algebras satisfying Poincaré duality, hard Lefschetz and Hodge index (the standard conjectures), connected with Kleiman's 1968 exposition.
errors: No real errors found. The products and the associativity identity check out: (xy)(tz)=[φ(x,y)φ(t,z)+Q(ψ(x,y),ψ(t,z))]ξ² because ξw=0.
The condition (xy)(tz)=(tx)(yz), combined with the built-in antisymmetries and pair-swap symmetry, is exactly antisymmetry under y↔t, hence full alternation. So the margin remark is correct.

Gap (not an error): the claim that this is the only associativity condition is stated without checking all triples. The other cases are indeed automatic given how H^1×H^2 and H^1×H^3 are defined by duality.
The Hodge/positivity condition (e.g. sign conditions on Q, positivity of φ relative to a Weil operator) is absent; the page stops at Lefschetz and Poincaré.

ideas.what: Classification of graded-commutative Poincaré-duality algebras of formal dimension 4 with a Lefschetz class, by data (V,W,φ,ψ,Q)
ideas.modern_name: Poincaré duality algebras with hard Lefschetz ('Kähler package' / Lefschetz algebras) of a surface type; analogous to classifying rational cohomology rings of 4-manifolds or Kähler surfaces
ideas.usually_credited_to: folklore; Lefschetz-algebra literature (Stanley, Watanabe et al.); Kleiman 1968 for the standard-conjecture axiomatics
ideas.where_published: Grothendieck's 'Standard conjectures on algebraic cycles' (1969) and Kleiman's 1968 exposition present the axioms but not, to my knowledge, this explicit low-dimensional model

ideas.what: Associativity in degree 4 is equivalent to the symmetric form (xy)(zt) on Λ²V being totally alternating, i.e. factoring through Λ⁴V
ideas.modern_name: Cup product Λ⁴H^1→H^4 factors through the exterior power; vanishing of the curvature-tensor part of a form in Sym²(Λ²V^∨)

ideas.what: Hard Lefschetz on H^1 is equivalent to nondegeneracy of φ; Poincaré duality on H^2 to nondegeneracy of Q
ideas.modern_name: Lefschetz / Poincaré conditions for a polarized Poincaré duality algebra

deep.surprise_reason: A clean but routine toy-model computation testing Grothendieck's Poincaré–Hodge algebra axioms in the surface case. It is interesting historically as a working example behind the standard-conjecture axiomatics, which anticipates the abstract 'Kähler package' later used in combinatorial Hodge theory. Mathematically it contains nothing a specialist would find new.
transcription_corrections: The crossed-out phrase before 'La connaissance de V,W,φ,ψ,Q…' is illegible; '[Pour les données]' is a guess.
In the i=2 line, the functional for xw is y↦Q(ψ(y,x),w) (with y,x in that order), as transcribed. The marginal list reads 'x∈V, y∈V, w∈W'.
Margin note reads approximately: 'exprime aussi que la forme (xy)(zt) en x,y,z,t est alternée (donc ne dépend que de xyzt!)'; the transcription is essentially right.
